main_text.p: dimus. Quam proximè igitur ad superius proximum epistolarum genus hoc accedit: ab eodem tamè differt, quod ibi præterita exponuntur: hîc verò, quæ futura indicantur.Sententiæ in denunciatoriis epistolis observandæ. Etsi autem, vt lib. epistolarum famil. 6. epist. 4. Cicero scribit, de futuris rebus semper difficile est dicere: tamen interdum coniectura possumus propius accedere, cum eiusmodi res est, cuius exitus prouideri queat. Etidem lib. 6. epist. epist. 6. futura se denunciare affirmat, non ex Astrologia, sed politica doctrina, usu, experientia, rerum ac temporum conditione. Nec nos quidem, inquit, nostra diuinatio fallet, quam tum sapientissimorum virorum monumentis atq; præceptis plurimoq; doctrinæ studio: tum magno etiam usu tractandæ Reip. magnaq; nostrorum temporum varietate consecuti sumus: cui quidem diuinationi hoc plus cõfidimus, q; ea nos nihil tam obscuris rebus tamq; perturbatis vnquā omnino fefellit. Itaq; sententiæ in hoc epistolarum genere sumentur, primum ex adiunctis, & circumstantiis personarum, loci, temporis, modi, causarum. Deinde testimoniis, & iudicio hominum communi, rumoribus qui spar-guntur: nostris etiam superioribus prædi-ctis.

page.notes: Printed "Etidem" in the first sentence after "lib. 6. epist." is kept as printed; it is probably a misprint for "Eidem". "epist. epist. 6." appears as printed, with the repeated "epist." at the line break. "fefellit" and "fe" (for se) are kept as printed. Marginal note text is partly italic and its hyphen is printed as "denunciato-riis". The printed "obferuandæ" is read as "observandæ" (the consonant v is set as v). The word "nostris" appears as "noftris" in the print; the long s is read as s.
